entries.value: The gatherings I've attended so far have come out of my own projects rather than a formal conference circuit. I was a national finalist at the Junior Science and Humanities Symposium for my Valley Fever work, where I presented an SIR-style epidemiological model I built in Python along with a microcontroller-based dust sensor I programmed in C/C++. More recently, ClarityAtlas, the iOS health product I lead technically at Open Health Intelligence, was selected for NSF I-Corps and the Johns Hopkins Pava Spark Accelerator, both of which involved cohort programming, customer discovery, and presenting to outside groups. Through that project I also presented to Johns Hopkins President Ron Daniels and leadership from the Hopkins Data Science and AI Institute. I don't have a confirmed conference schedule for this year yet, but the events most likely to reach people like me are university accelerator demo days, NSF I-Corps cohorts, and Hopkins Data Science and AI Institute events, since those are where students who are actually shipping products tend to show up.
